question: What is the primary layer of the heart affected in infective endocarditis?
explanation: Endocarditis specifically targets the endocardial tissue, which includes the inner lining of the heart chambers and the heart valves. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T6#GNS213_U1_T6_h1)

question: Myocarditis differs from endocarditis because myocarditis primarily involves which structure?
explanation: Myocarditis is an inflammation of the myocardium, which is the muscular middle layer responsible for heart contraction. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T6#GNS213_U1_T6_h1)

question: What are the infected masses called that form on heart valves during endocarditis?
explanation: Microorganisms combine with platelets and fibrin to form clumps of tissue on the valves called vegetations. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T6#GNS213_U1_T6_h2)

question: A patient with suspected endocarditis presents with painful nodules on their fingertips. What are these called?
explanation: Osler's nodes are tender, painful subcutaneous lesions found on the pads of fingers and toes in infective endocarditis. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T6#GNS213_U1_T6_h2)

question: Which pathogen type is the most common worldwide cause of myocarditis?
explanation: Viral infections, especially enteroviruses like Coxsackievirus, are the leading cause of heart muscle inflammation. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T6#GNS213_U1_T6_h3)

question: Why can myocarditis present with chest pain similar to a heart attack?

options.D: Plaque ruptures inside the main aorta

explanation: Inflammatory swelling and cellular damage in the heart wall cause chest discomfort even without blocked coronary blood vessels. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T6#GNS213_U1_T6_h3)

question: What position typically relieves the sharp chest pain associated with acute pericarditis?

options.A: Lying flat flat on the back
options.B: Turning completely to the left side

explanation: Leaning forward pulls the heart away from the parietal pleura, reducing friction and easing the pain. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T6#GNS213_U1_T6_h4)

question: A pericardial friction rub heard during auscultation is best described as what kind of sound?
explanation: The inflamed layers of the pericardium rub against each other during movement, creating a characteristic scratchy sound. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T6#GNS213_U1_T6_h4)

question: Which diagnostic tool is most effective for visualizing heart valve vegetations?
explanation: Ultrasound imaging of the heart allows clinicians to directly view vegetation clumps attached to valve leaflets. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T6#GNS213_U1_T6_h5)

question: Why are multiple sets of blood cultures drawn from different sites for suspected endocarditis?

options.A: To check if the kidneys are filtering blood adequately
options.B: To measure total red blood cell volume in circulation
options.C: To test for resistance against common antiviral medications
options.D: To confirm continuous bacteremia and rule out skin contaminants

explanation: Drawing blood from separate sites helps prove bacteria are actively circulating in the bloodstream rather than being accidental skin contaminants. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T6#GNS213_U1_T6_h5)

question: What is the typical duration of intravenous antibiotic therapy required for infective endocarditis?
explanation: Eradicating bacteria hidden deep inside valve vegetations requires a prolonged course of targeted intravenous antibiotics. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T6#GNS213_U1_T6_h6)

question: What medication is commonly added to NSAIDs to prevent the recurrence of acute pericarditis?
explanation: Colchicine is an anti-inflammatory drug that significantly lowers the rate of recurrent pericarditis episodes when combined with NSAIDs. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T6#GNS213_U1_T6_h6)

question: Which condition is a primary indication for surgical intervention in infective endocarditis?

options.A: Low-grade fever lasting only two days
options.B: Severe valve failure causing heart failure
options.C: A slight elevation in white blood cells
options.D: Mild fatigue during routine morning walks

explanation: Structural damage to heart valves that causes acute heart failure requires prompt surgical repair or replacement. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T6#GNS213_U1_T6_h7)

question: A patient with pericardial effusion develops muffled heart sounds and low blood pressure. What urgent procedure is anticipated?
explanation: Pericardiocentesis involves draining fluid from the pericardial sac to relieve pressure during cardiac tamponade. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T6#GNS213_U1_T6_h7)

question: Why is late clinical presentation a major challenge in managing cardiac infections within many Nigerian settings?

options.A: Patients refuse to take prescribed intravenous medications entirely
options.B: Advanced tissue damage and complications have already developed
options.C: Local diagnostic machines cannot detect bacteria in blood cultures
options.D: Laboratory reagents are universally unavailable in every clinic

explanation: Delayed presentation means patients often arrive when heart valve destruction or heart failure is already advanced, complicating treatment. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T6#GNS213_U1_T6_h8)

question: What preventive advice should a nurse give a patient who has recovered from infective endocarditis before a dental procedure?

options.A: Avoid all forms of dental hygiene care for at least six months
options.B: Take strong pain relievers immediately before entering the dental clinic
options.C: Request general anesthesia instead of local numbing injections
options.D: Discuss the need for pre-procedure antibiotic prophylaxis with your doctor

explanation: High-risk patients often require prophylactic antibiotics prior to dental work that manipulates gingival tissue to prevent recurrent bacteremia. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T6#GNS213_U1_T6_h8)
